og.title: Air Movers for Professional Restoration | CARSI
og.description: Choose and place air movers with confidence. Covers airflow, static pressure and lift, axial versus centrifugal versus low-profile selection, placement and quantity by class of loss, and amps, GPOs and scaling on 230 V power.

keywords: class of loss air mover placement

faq.q: What does this air mover course cover?
faq.a: It covers airflow, static pressure and lift; axial, centrifugal and low-profile selection; placement and quantity by class of loss; amps, GPOs and scaling; clean, grey, sewage and mould conditions; and buying plus on-site assessment.

faq.q: Is this course written for Australian conditions?
faq.a: Yes. It is written for the Australian market throughout, using 230 V / 50 Hz power, 10 A GPOs, metric units, and equipment available in Australia as at July 2026.

faq.q: Should low-profile air movers be my main drying equipment?
faq.a: No. The course makes this its through-line: low-profile units have a place, but they should not be the primary air mover for a professional firm. The aim is to match the air mover to the job.

faq.q: How much does this course cost?
faq.a: It is free to enrol. The live course page lists it as a free course, so you can start it without paying.
